source: dos/mscode.asm Win386_Msg and OldWin386Init; inc/lmstub.asm OldInstanceJunk
findings: The corresponding target INT 2Fh AH=16h dispatch checks AL=6, AL=7, then AL=5; for AL=3 it falls through to the next-handler jump.
The DOS 6 baseline explicitly checks AL=3 and routes it to OldWin386Init, which returns the OldInstanceJunk table and AX=5248h.
No B8 48 52 instruction encoding or baseline OldInstanceJunk six-byte header occurs anywhere in target IO.SYS.
These observations support the conclusion that this old WIN386 2.x dispatch path was removed from the target; they do not independently establish all references to the altah byte.
limitations: Absence of a byte sequence alone cannot exclude a differently encoded equivalent path.
Other indirect uses, remaining Windows compatibility code and exact target kernel data layout need separate verification.
No complete source reconstruction or linked target kernel is established.
